hero.eyebrow: Mutual aid in Marietta and metro Atlanta
hero.headline: Free repairs for neighbors who can’t afford them.
hero.lede: A broken window, a leaking sink, a car that won’t start. Small things that turn into a crisis when there’s no money to fix them. C3 pairs people who need a repair with volunteers who have the tools and skills to do it. No income verification.
intro.heading: Neighbors with tools, helping neighbors without them.
intro.p1: Everyone has the right to a better tomorrow, and no one should be denied the repairs and resources that make daily life livable. When things start falling apart it can be catastrophic for families already at the margins — and most of us no longer have an emergency fund for a water heater or a brake job.
intro.p2: C3 brings together artists, craftspeople, tradespeople and anyone willing to lend a hand, and works alongside public, private and faith organizations to get those repairs done — free, for the people who need them most.
services.heading: What we fix
services.intro: Six kinds of work, all free for the people who need them. Not sure your problem fits? Ask anyway.
services.1.title: Home repairs & maintenance
services.1.text: Drywall, doors, windows, locks, outlets and switches, leaks, flooring — the everyday fixes that keep a house safe and livable.
services.2.title: Auto repairs
services.2.text: Brakes, batteries, belts, A/C and other minor repairs that keep you getting to work and the kids getting to school.
services.3.title: Emergency repairs
services.3.text: Burst pipes, broken water heaters, a window that won’t close before a cold snap. When it can’t wait, tell us.
services.4.title: Landscaping
services.4.text: Overgrown yards, dangerous limbs, drainage and access problems that make a home harder to live in.
services.5.title: Junk removal
services.5.text: Clearing out debris, old appliances and hazards so a home or yard is usable again.
services.6.title: Appliance repair
services.6.text: Refrigerators, window A/C units, washers and dryers — repaired when possible, replaced when we can source one.
steps.heading: How it works
steps.intro: Seven questions, no income verification. We’re new and volunteer-run, so please be patient — we’ll get to your project as quickly as we can.
steps.1.title: Tell us what’s broken
steps.1.text: Fill out the short request form — what needs fixing, a few photos, and how it’s affecting your day-to-day. Takes about five minutes.
steps.2.title: We match you with a volunteer
steps.2.text: A tradesperson, handyman or crew in your area picks up the job. We try to group projects by neighborhood so we can help several households in a weekend.
steps.3.title: The repair gets done
steps.3.text: Materials are covered by donations and by paying customers who choose to fund a neighbor’s repair. You pay nothing.
band.caption: “Universal compassion leads us to the conviction that all humans are deserving of basic needs and dignity.”
doors.help.title: Request help
doors.help.text: Home, auto, emergency, landscaping, junk removal, appliances. Tell us what’s wrong and attach a few photos.
doors.volunteer.title: Volunteer
doors.volunteer.text: Trades, tools, a truck, a weekend, or a skill you want to learn. Georgia, we need your help.
events.heading: Upcoming events
events.intro: Free pantry builds, food distribution days, benefit shows, art and craft days.
partners.heading: Who we work with
partners.intro: Mutual aid groups, collectives and community networks we organize alongside across Georgia.

mission.quote: We believe unconditional compassion is the bridge to working together across religion, race, ideology and culture.
mission.text: C3, Creative Collaboration for Compassion, is an initiative that brings together the creativity of artists, craftspeople, creators and anyone willing, to benefit others by providing quality-of-life repairs and resources. We are committed to a vision of unity through community service and mutual aid for those less fortunate.
about.lede: C3 started in early 2025 as a conversation between a carpenter, a local pastor, and a chatbot. It became a window repair that October, funded with materials from a local school system — and a lot of people asking how they could help.
about.why.heading: Why repairs?
about.why.p1: Everyone has the right to a better tomorrow, and no one should be denied quality-of-life repairs and resources. When things start falling apart it can be catastrophic for families already at the margins. Most Americans no longer have the emergency funds for a repair or a medical bill — a broken water heater or a car that won’t start isn’t an inconvenience, it’s a crisis.
about.why.p2: Our hope is to provide those repairs and resources for free, by bridging divides and working with a variety of public, private and religious organizations. We believe that serving someone else, side by side, is the fastest way to soften hearts and build the bridges this moment needs.
about.who.heading: Who’s behind it
about.who.p1: C3 was founded by a Marietta craftsman with more than 20 years in custom construction, woodworking and remodeling. He closed his woodworking business in the fall of 2024 after the challenges of the COVID years, and decided the knowledge, talent and tools he’d built up were worth more in service than in storage.
about.who.p2: Since the idea went public, dozens of people have offered to help — including with this website. If you’re one of them, the volunteer form is the fastest way to plug in.
about.partners.heading: Partners & affiliates
about.partners.text: We organize alongside mutual aid groups, collectives and community networks across Georgia.
about.next.heading: What’s next
about.next.p1: Beyond repairs, we’re putting together community art days, art & craft shows, little free pantries and libraries, potlucks and food distribution, and self-sustaining skill-building workshops. A poetry collection on compassion, cooperation and shared responsibility is in the works — fifty poets, three poems each, all proceeds to quality-of-life repairs.
loop.heading: How the free repairs get paid for
loop.intro: Until donations can carry the program on their own, C3 runs on a pay-it-forward loop. If you can afford a handyman, hiring us funds a repair for a neighbor who can’t.
loop.1.title: Someone hires us
loop.1.text: A homeowner who can pay books a handyman or repair job at a fair rate.
loop.2.title: Proceeds are set aside
loop.2.text: Earnings from that job go toward materials for a free repair.
loop.3.title: A neighbor gets help
loop.3.text: A volunteer completes a quality-of-life repair for someone at the margins — at no cost.
loop.4.title: Partners multiply it
loop.4.text: Churches, schools, collectives and businesses match funds, donate materials or send hands.
loop.outro: Can’t cover the full cost of your own repair, but want to contribute? Tell us on the request form — we may be able to discount your project and turn it into a funding project for someone else.
donate.lede: Every dollar goes to materials for quality-of-life repairs. Every bag of groceries, box of screws or Saturday morning goes just as far.
donate.money.title: Give money
donate.money.text: Materials are the main cost of a free repair — a window sash, a water heater, a set of brake pads. Donations are collected through our GoFundMe for now.
donate.materials.title: Give materials & resources
donate.materials.text: Lumber, hardware, appliances in working order, tools you no longer use. We also collect food, clothing and medicine for distribution days with our partners.
donate.time.title: Give time
donate.time.text: Trades, a truck, a strong back, or a skill you’d like to learn. Businesses: pro-bono or low-cost services go straight into the program.
donate.where.heading: Where your donation goes
donate.where.p1: We want to be inclusive and build bridges, and we’re open to helping most anyone. If you’d like your gift directed toward a particular community — veterans, the elderly, people with disabilities, single parents, immigrants, people in recovery or re-entering after incarceration — let us know and we’ll do our best to honor it.
donate.where.p2: Organizations: if you’d like to match funds on a project, help determine the recipient, or send a crew, we’d love to partner.
donate.hire.heading: Hire us, fund a neighbor
donate.hire.text: Need handyman or repair work and able to pay for it? Hiring C3 at a fair rate directly funds a free repair for someone who can’t. More than 20 years of construction, woodworking and remodeling experience, and every job pays forward.
contact.heading: Questions, ideas, partnerships
contact.lede: Need a repair or want to volunteer? Use the Get involved forms — they go to the right place faster. For everything else, write to us here.
contact.card1.title: Reach us directly
contact.card2.title: Know someone who needs help?
contact.card2.text: Tell us about them. A lot of the people who need a repair most are the last to ask for one.
contact.card2.link: Submit a request on their behalf
contact.card3.title: Organizations
contact.card3.text: Want to match funds, donate materials or co-host a project day? We’re actively looking for partners.
involved.help.tabsub: Request free help — 7 questions, no income verification
involved.help.heading: Request help
involved.help.lede: Thank you for reaching out. Please take a minute to answer a few questions so we can maximize the impact of this program. No income verification — we trust you. If you’re asking on behalf of someone else, that’s welcome too.
involved.help.thanks: Thank you so much for reaching out.
involved.help.thankstext: We hope we can help with your repair soon. This is a new initiative we’re working to get off the ground, so please be patient — we’ll do our best to get to your project in a timely manner.
involved.volunteer.tabsub: Volunteer skills, tools, time or resources
involved.volunteer.heading: Volunteer
involved.volunteer.lede: Georgia, we need your help. If you’re a tradesperson, a handyman, own a business that can offer pro-bono or low-cost work, or just want to learn a skill and lend a hand — tell us a little about yourself and we’ll plug you in.
involved.volunteer.thankstext: We’ll be in touch as projects come up that fit your skills and area. In the meantime, follow us on Instagram to see what’s happening.
faq.q1: Who qualifies for a free repair?
faq.a1: Anyone whose quality of life is being hurt by something they can’t afford to fix. There is no income verification — we ask you to tell us a little about your situation on the request form, and we trust you. We’re a small, new program, so we prioritize the people in the most need and try to get to everyone we can.
faq.q2: What kinds of repairs do you do?
faq.a2: Home repairs and maintenance, auto repairs, emergency repairs, landscaping, junk removal and appliance repair. Broken windows, locks, outlets and switches, leaky sinks, water heaters, window A/C units, refrigerators, minor auto repairs — inquiries are always welcome, even if your problem isn’t on the list.
faq.a3: This is a volunteer-run initiative getting off the ground over the course of the spring and summer. Please be patient; we’ll get to your project as quickly as we can and we’ll keep you posted. Emergencies (no water, no heat, a home that can’t be secured) go first.
faq.q4: Do I have to share my address?
faq.a4: Not up front. Tell us the general area and we’ll ask for an exact address only once we’re ready to move forward. We often try to help several households in one area over a weekend.
faq.q5: I can pay for part of my repair. Does that help?
faq.a5: Yes. If you want to contribute but can’t cover the whole cost, we may be able to discount your project — and turn it into a funding project for another neighbor or a community event. Mention it on the request form.
faq.q6: How are the free repairs funded?
faq.a6: Right now, mostly by paid handyman work: when someone who can afford it hires C3, the proceeds buy materials for a free repair. Partner organizations contribute materials and matching funds, and donations come in through our GoFundMe. The goal is for donations to carry the program over time.
faq.q7: I’m a contractor or business. How do I help?
faq.a7: Fill out the volunteer form and tell us your trade, your availability and whether you can offer pro-bono or low-cost work. Businesses can also donate materials, match funds on a project, or help choose a recipient in their community.
faq.a8: C3 is a new community initiative based in Marietta, Georgia, working alongside established mutual aid groups and organizations. Contact us if you need details for a grant, a match or an in-kind donation.
footer.cta.heading: Need a repair? Have skills to share?
footer.cta.text: Tell us what’s broken, or tell us what you can do. Either way, you’re part of this.
